summary: SAML attribute with semicolon-delimited groups parsed as single group on API path; service-account impersonation denied in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after onboarding via SAML SSO, scheduled worker jobs and API impersonation calls for a particular service account are failing with 403 'insufficient_scope' or 403 'unauthorized_impersonation'. The same SAML assertion, when used to log in to the Redwood Console, shows the expected group memberships in the Console UI and admin role is visible. The failure appears only for API routes and scheduled worker impersonation, not interactive console sessions.

Impact:
- Several scheduled batch jobs (daily model scoring) failed to start for the last 6 hours.
- Customer's service account cannot be used for impersonation endpoints; operational impact to production analytics pipelines.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) running identity-proxy v1.18.2 behind HAProxy ingress in eu-west.
- SAML IdP: Customer on-prem ADFS 2019, sending Groups attribute as a single string with semicolon separators (e.g., "GroupA;GroupB;org-admins").

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger SAML SSO via IdP, capture SAML Response (POST with Groups attribute as semicolon-delimited string).
2) Login via Console -> groups render as: ["GroupA","GroupB","org-admins"].
3) Call /v1/impersonate using same session cookie or SAML-backed token -> 403 with message 'service account role missing'.
4) Inspect headers arriving at identity-proxy for API path vs console path; API path contains header 'x-rw-groups: GroupA;GroupB;org-admins' (single header value), while console flow has header passed through as multiple header instances in the HTTP stack.

Observed behavior:
- API path: RBAC evaluation treats the entire 'GroupA;GroupB;org-admins' string as a single group label, no match to configured role bindings.
- Console path: framework shows parsed groups correctly (console route normalizes header by splitting on both comma and semicolon).

Expected behavior:
- Both console and API routes should parse group attributes similarly and match against role bindings so impersonation succeeds when the user is in any required group.

Relevant logs/traces (redacted):
- identity-proxy (api route) at 2026-03-11T09:17:22Z: "received header x-rw-groups=GroupA;GroupB;org-admins"
- rbac-evaluator (api route) at 2026-03-11T09:17:22Z: "no matching role binding for subject 'GroupA;GroupB;org-admins'"
- console-auth (same timestamp): "parsed groups [\"GroupA\",\"GroupB\",\"org-admins\"] for user uid=aurora"

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Updated IdP to emit groups as multiple attribute instances (not possible for all groups due to IdP config limits).
- Temporary role binding created for literal group string "GroupA;GroupB;org-admins" to restore impersonation while we investigate.
comments: Support (2026-03-11 10:02 UTC) - Asha Menon: Acknowledged, escalating to identity team; collecting packet capture and sample SAML response. SLA updated to P1.
Customer (2026-03-11 11:15 UTC) - Helena Park (Aurora): Provided SAML response and HAProxy config snippet. Confirmed console flows show expected groups; API flows do not.

SRE (2026-03-11 14:43 UTC) - Diego Ramos: Verified ingress rewrites multiple header instances into a single header value for backend API routes due to 'http-request set-header' config in HAProxy. This explains why API path sees single header value. Will pair with identity team to confirm parsing difference.

Identity Eng (2026-03-12 08:22 UTC) - Liam O'Connor: Reproduced locally with a test IdP emitting semicolon-delimited groups. Found identity-proxy's header-splitting logic only splits on comma for API auth path; console path uses a shared middleware that splits on comma and semicolon. Preparing patch to unify parsing behavior.

Customer (2026-03-12 12:01 UTC) - Helena Park: Applied temporary role binding for the semicolon-joined literal and restored scheduled jobs. Requesting permanent fix and guidance to avoid future breaks.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Packet capture shows HAProxy collapsing multiple Set-Cookie and multiple x-rw-groups instances into a single header string when using 'http-request set-header' with concatenation. This is common in their HAProxy config to normalize incoming headers for backend routing.

2026-03-12: identity-proxy v1.18.2 has divergent code paths: 'console' flow runs middleware 'parseGroupAttributeExtended' which splits on /[,;\s]+/, but 'api' flow uses older util 'splitCsv' that only splits on commas and trims whitespace. Unit tests missed semicolon-only delimiter cases.

Hypothesis: The combination of ingress header concatenation (producing a semicolon-separated single header) and the api-path-only CSV parser leads to the observed RBAC miss. Explanation aligns with customer reproduction and logs.

Impact assessment: Any private deployment behind an ingress that concatenates headers and any IdP that uses semicolons as group separators could be affected. Likely low incidence but high impact when it hits scheduled/impersonation flows.
Related: similar header-normalization issues referenced in SUP-412998 (oauth2 introspection csv->json) but different delimiter semantics; recorded for cross-reference.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: created a customer-scoped role binding for the literal semicolon-joined group string to restore operations. Permanent fix: landed and staged identity-proxy patch that unifies group parsing logic to split on commas, semicolons, and whitespace (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/5742). Deployed v1.19.0 to staging on 2026-03-12 and rolled to customer private environment on 2026-03-13 during a maintenance window. Verified impersonation and scheduled jobs succeed post-deploy. Follow-ups: (1) Add unit tests for semicolon-only group lists and header-concatenation scenarios, (2) Update SAML mapping guidance in Confluence to recommend emitting groups as separate attributes when possible, and (3) Add an identity-proxy telemetry metric to surface header-splitting anomalies. Documentation PR created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IDP/SAML+Attribute+Mapping+Guidance#HeaderDelimiterHandling.
